chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Abu Dawud al-Mustarriq and from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I apply kohl containing musk while I am fasting.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl with musk break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that applying kohl containing musk does not invalidate the fast, addressing the juristic debate on whether substances entering the eye are considered 'food' or 'drink'. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that minor sensory absorptions, unlike substantial ingestion, do not break the fast, providing practical guidance for daily worship. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufi school of hadith in preserving these specific legal nuances.
